items.title: Hybrid nanocrystal surface reveals new way to tune interactions with infrared light
items.summary: A one-crystal-thick sheet made from two types of nanocrystals mixed in solution can amplify or suppress infrared light beyond the sum of its parts.

items.summary: A team of researchers, including those from the University of Tokyo, have developed a new way to model the Milky Way at a level of detail never achieved before. items.title: Parasite makes mice more attractive to blood-feeding bugs, which may aid its spread
items.summary: Some parasites, such as Trypanosoma rangeli and Trypanosoma cruzi, can be passed between mammals and blood-feeding insects called triatomine bugs. Bugs can acquire these parasites when feeding on infected mammals, while mammals can also become infected through encounters with infected bugs.

items.title: Repeated bending strengthens sugar-based hydrogel instead of wearing it down
items.summary: Most materials get weaker with use. But a team led by Chenfeng Ke, a professor of chemistry in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis, has created a polymer that defies the usual laws of wear and tear.

items.title: Babies in ancient Greek colony started solid food at 3 months but nursed for nearly 4 years, chemical signatures suggest
items.summary: Over 2,500 years ago, Himera was a Greek colony inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks. Despite their diverse cultural backgrounds, they all shared one thing: they began weaning their babies early and continued for a long time.
